questions.q: Why does this capstone deliberately avoid building the Board's Tableau deck on Sample - Superstore, the dataset bundled with Tableau?
options: Superstore is too large to load in Tableau Desktop
The Board wants real Thornbury numbers checkable against Power BI and Excel, and Superstore would defeat the entire 'one source of truth' premise this capstone is built around
Superstore cannot be joined to a SQL Server connection
Tableau no longer ships with Sample - Superstore
questions.explain: If the Tableau deck used a different dataset, nothing in it could ever be reconciled against the Power BI dashboard or Finance's workbook — breaking the whole point of a shared warehouse.

questions.q: Which Tableau connector is used to reach the warehouse, and what does that connection actually open?
options: A text file connector, importing a one-time CSV export
The Microsoft SQL Server connector, opening a live connection to the actual dw.* schema — not a copy or export
The Google Sheets connector
Tableau's built-in sample data connector
questions.explain: Tableau's native Microsoft SQL Server connector reaches the same database Power BI and the Python validation script already connect to.

questions.q: How are the four joins on the Data Source tab configured, and what do they mirror?
options: Four left joins, mirroring an entirely new relationship structure
Four inner joins from dw.FactProductSales to each dimension on its surrogate key, mirroring the exact star schema the warehouse's own load defined
One single join combining all five tables into a flattened view
No joins are needed since Tableau auto-detects relationships
questions.explain: Each join matches the warehouse's own T-SQL join logic from Chapter 2 — ProductKey, OrderDateKey/DateKey, TerritoryKey, and CustomerKey — expressed as Tableau joins instead of SQL.

questions.q: What does a Live connection mean in Tableau, as used in this lesson, versus an Extract?
options: A Live connection queries the warehouse directly on every interaction, keeping the deck current with every refresh; an Extract is a saved, potentially stale snapshot
A Live connection only works with cloud databases
An Extract is always faster and more accurate than a Live connection
There is no practical difference between the two
questions.explain: Live connections query the source directly each time, which keeps this deck in sync with the warehouse's nightly refresh, unlike a one-time Extract snapshot.

questions.q: Why does the lab's final check — comparing SUM(LineTotal) in Tableau to [Total Sales] in Power BI — matter this early in Chapter 5?
options: It's just a formatting exercise with no real significance
It's the first real cross-tool check in this capstone, confirming the Tableau connection is actually reading the same real data Power BI reads
It replaces the need for Chapter 3's Python validation
It only matters once the Excel workbook is built in Chapter 6
questions.explain: Confirming the two totals match for the same period is the earliest proof that this capstone's 'one source of truth' architecture is actually holding, before any further Tableau work is built on top of it.
